findings.claim: The new `scrollIntoView` in `pick()` has no test. It is the only thing that brings an arrow-selected card into view once the row scrolls, and it is supposed to do that without moving the page. Deleting the line, or swapping `block: 'nearest'` for `block: 'start'`, leaves every test passing.
findings.evidence: Added at start-screen.ts:52: `card.element.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' });`. No test in tests/ calls scrollIntoView or presses an arrow key in 'track-select--many-cards'. The only tests with ArrowRight are pine-ridge-lock.test.ts, track-select.test.ts and track-select-modifier-keys.test.ts, all four-card setups where nothing scrolls. AC2 sets `row.scrollLeft` directly and never selects a card. Mutation: delete line 52. In the eight-card stage at 844×390, focus Dust Bowl and press ArrowLeft, which wraps to the last fixture card (index 7, off-screen right). The focused, checked card stays outside the row's visible box, and every test still passes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test in a new file that renders 'track-select--many-cards' at 844×390 (touch) and focuses the checked radio. Press ArrowLeft so the selection wraps to the last card. Assert the new aria-checked radio's box lies within the radiogroup's box (reuse `within` and `rowState` from track-select-many-cards.test.ts), `window.scrollY` is unchanged, and `documentElement.scrollWidth` ≤ 844.

findings.claim: Nothing tests that unlocked cards behave as before, meaning no shake and no swallowed Enter/Space. Dropping the `!locked ||` guard makes Enter/Space shake an unlocked card and call preventDefault on it, and the tests stay green. Making click shake every card survives too.
findings.evidence: track-card.ts:75-79: `element.addEventListener('click', () => (locked ? shakeLocked() : onPick()));` and `if (!locked || (e.key !== 'Enter' && e.key !== ' ') || ...) return; e.preventDefault(); shakeLocked();`. Every new test targets only the locked radio: `pine(page)` in locked-card-shake.test.ts and `[aria-disabled="true"]` in locked-card-rest.test.ts. AC7 only hovers Dust Bowl and never clicks it or presses a key on it. Mutation A: change line 76 to `if ((e.key !== 'Enter' && e.key !== ' ') || e.altKey || ...) return;`. Focus Dust Bowl in 'start--menu' and press Enter: `getAnimations().length` is 1 (a shake). No test fails. Mutation B: change line 75 to `() => { shakeLocked(); if (!locked) onPick(); }`. Clicking Dust Bowl now shakes it, and no test fails. The plan audit requires 'Handle Enter/Space only for locked cards. Unlocked cards and arrow keys behave as before.'
findings.suggestedFix: In a new test, in 'start--menu' at 1440×900, click an unlocked radio (Dust Bowl). Focus it and press Enter, then Space. After each, assert `el.getAnimations().filter(a => !(a instanceof CSSTransition)).length === 0`. For the keys, also assert the keydown was not default-prevented: dispatch a cancelable KeyboardEvent and check that `dispatchEvent` returns true.

findings.claim: The spec says Enter/Space on a locked card calls preventDefault, but no test checks that. AC4 compares scrollY and scrollLeft, and neither moves on this layout whether or not the default is prevented, so deleting `e.preventDefault()` survives.
findings.evidence: track-card.ts:78: `e.preventDefault();`. AC4 (locked-card-shake.test.ts) compares `[window.scrollY, radiogroup.scrollLeft]` before and after Enter/Space. The 'start--menu' page fits 844×390 and doesn't scroll vertically. The row has `overflow-y: hidden`, and Space's default action scrolls vertically, so the tuple stays the same with or without preventDefault. Mutation: delete line 78. All of AC4 still passes: the shake comes from the handler, focus stays, and the scroll tuple is unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test that focuses Pine Ridge and dispatches `new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: ' ', bubbles: true, cancelable: true })`, then the same with key 'Enter'. Assert `dispatchEvent` returns false (defaultPrevented), and that a plain ArrowRight on an unlocked card still moves the selection.

checked.how: Checks exact keyframes [[0,0],[4,0],[-4,0],[4,0],[0,0]], duration 250, bezier [0.2,0.9,0.3,1], fill none/auto, both signs, y=0, finish at identity, and aria-checked unchanged, in both click and tap contexts. Changing a constant in SHAKE or SHAKE_TIMING fails it.
Mutation: remove `shake?.cancel()` (track-card.ts:72). Three synchronous clicks then give counts [1,2,3] instead of [1,1,1], so the test fails. The Enter loop fails the same way.

A control click with motion allowed shows one animation first, so the test isn't vacuous. Mutation: drop the `reducedMotion() ? null :` branch and the reduced-motion clicks animate, so the test fails.
Hover and press keep the rest pose (this already holds on main). The release-shake assertions (count 1, duration 250) fail on main, as the plan audit asked. The unlocked hover-lift check is there.

Each test checks: 8 radios, snap-type x, scrollbar none, snap-align ≠ none, width 96±0.5, a peek card that straddles the row edge, name lines inside the card (≤2 lines), RACE's box unchanged after scrolling to the end, the last card within the row, docWidth ≤844. Mutating min-width or scroll-snap-align fails them.
sampleShake pauses the animation and seeks currentTime, so the samples are deterministic and don't depend on wall-clock timing. finishShake finishes every animation before reading the transform.
